title: Cycles of the four-digit Kaprekar map in even bases
abstract: The four-digit Kaprekar map in base B sends an integer 0 <= x < B^4, written with four base-B digits (leading zeros allowed), to the descending arrangement of its digits minus the ascending arrangement. A cycle is a periodic orbit through an input whose digits are not all equal. Cycles are counted up to cyclic shift, including fixed points of least period one. This formalization uses only Lean 4 core and Std and proves Theorem 1 of R. Galyavin, "Cycles of the four-digit Kaprekar map in even bases" (2026). For B = m*2^n with m odd, n >= 1 and m >= 5, each cycle of the folded map on odd difference pairs lifts to a cycle of the same length. There is one additional cycle of length n+1 if 2^n is 1 modulo m, or one of length 2(n+1) if m = 5 and n is 2 modulo 4. The two conditions are mutually exclusive and the list is exhaustive. For m = 3, odd n gives one cycle of length 3(n+1), and even n gives two cycles of lengths n+1 and 2(n+1). Base two has two fixed points. In base 2^n for odd n >= 3 there are (n-1)/2 cycles of each length n and n+2. For even n >= 2 there are (n-2)/2 cycles of each of those lengths, one of length n/2 and one of length n/2+1. The map is stated directly as digit sorting and subtraction on natural numbers.
